catalytic_activity: CATALYTIC ACTIVITY: Reaction=L-oxindolylalanine + L-leucyl-(O-isoindolinone)-L-homoserine + ATP = L-Leu-L-Isd-L-Oid + AMP + diphosphate + H(+); Xref=Rhea:RHEA:85803, ChEBI:CHEBI:15378, ChEBI:CHEBI:30616, ChEBI:CHEBI:33019, ChEBI:CHEBI:234545, ChEBI:CHEBI:234550, ChEBI:CHEBI:234551, ChEBI:CHEBI:456215; Evidence={ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549}; PhysiologicalDirection=left-to-right; Xref=Rhea:RHEA:85804; Evidence={ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549};
function: FUNCTION: Amide-bond synthetase; part of the coc gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of isoindolinone-containing peptide natural products (PubMed:40387549). Within the pathway, cocJ combines an L-oxindolylalanine (L-Oid) residue to the dipeptide L-Leu-L-Isd to produce the tripeptide L-Leu-L-Isd-L-oxindolylalanine (PubMed:40387549). The alanine racemase cocA first catalyzes the interconversion between L-alanine and D-alanine. D-alanine is then activated by the NRPS cocH that transfers it to the PKS cocB to produce R-dihydroxymethyl isoindolinone. CocG then catalyzes the gamma-replacement of acetate in O-acetyl-L-homoserine (OAH) with R-dihydroxymethyl isoindolinone to generate the amino acid L-O-isoindolinone-homoserine (L-Isd). Then, the ATP-grasp enzyme cocI acts as an amide-bond-forming enzyme that activates the carboxylate of L-Leu for condensation with the amino group in L-Isd to give the dipeptide L-Leu-L-Isd. CocJ then adds an L-oxindolylalanine (L-Oid) residue to L-Leu-L-Isd to produce L-Leu-L-Isd-L-oxindolylalanine. L-Oid is produced by cocE via oxindole formation on L-Trp. The final peptide natural product of the coc BGC remains undetermined and the functions of the cytochrome P450 monooxygenase cocC and the FMN oxidoreductase cocF still need to be determined (PubMed:40387549). {ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549}.

catalytic_activity: CATALYTIC ACTIVITY: Reaction=L-leucyl-(O-isoindolinone)-D-homoserine + L-alanyl-L-glutamine + ATP = L-Leu-D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln + AMP + diphosphate + H(+); Xref=Rhea:RHEA:85791, ChEBI:CHEBI:15378, ChEBI:CHEBI:30616, ChEBI:CHEBI:33019, ChEBI:CHEBI:74387, ChEBI:CHEBI:234547, ChEBI:CHEBI:234548, ChEBI:CHEBI:456215; Evidence={ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549}; PhysiologicalDirection=left-to-right; Xref=Rhea:RHEA:85792; Evidence={ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549};
function: FUNCTION: Amide-bond synthetase; part of the unc gene cluster that mediates the biosynthesis of the tripeptide D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln called isoindolamide B (PubMed:40387549). Within the pathway, uncG combines the L-Leu-D-Isd dipeptide with the L-Ala-L-Gln dipeptide to yield the tetrapeptide L-Leu-D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln (PubMed:40387549). The alanine racemase uncE first catalyzes the interconversion between L-alanine and D-alanine. D-alanine is then activated by the NRPS uncD that transfers it to the PKS uncA to produce R-dihydroxymethyl isoindolinone. UncF then catalyzes the gamma-replacement of acetate in O-acetyl-L-homoserine (OAH) with R-dihydroxymethyl isoindolinone to generate the amino acid L-O-isoindolinone-homoserine (L-Isd). Then, the ATP-grasp enzyme uncK acts as an amide-bond-forming enzyme that activates the carboxylate of L-Leu for condensation with the amino group in L-Isd to give the dipeptide L-Leu-L-Isd. Epimerase uncI converts L-Leu-L-Isd to L-Leu-D-Isd in which C-alpha of the Isd residue is epimerized from L to D. UncH is able to hydrolyze dipeptides L-Leu-L-Isd or L-Leu-D-Isd to yield L-Isd or D-Isd, respectively, along with L-Leu. UncG then produces the tetrapeptide L-Leu-D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln by adding L-Ala-L-Gln produced by the dipeptide synthetase uncJ that forms L-Ala-L-Gln from L-Ala and L-Gln. Finally, hydrolysis of L-Leu-D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln by uncH leads to the final tripeptide D-Isd-L-Ala-L-Gln called isoindolamide B (PubMed:40387549). {ECO:0000269|PubMed:40387549}.

function: FUNCTION: ATP-grasp enzyme involved in the synthesis of cell surface polysaccharides (PubMed:25368324). function: FUNCTION: Part of the bacABCDEFG operon responsible for the biosynthesis of bacilysin, an irreversible inactivator of the glutaminase domain of glucosamine synthetase. Catalyzes the formation of alpha-dipeptides from various L-amino acids in the presence of ATP. In vivo catalyzes the ligation of L-alanine and L-anticapsin (epoxycyclohexanonyl-Ala) to produce the final bacilysin antibiotic (L-Ala-L-4S-cyclohexenonyl-Ala dipeptide). The substrate specificity is restricted to small amino acids such as L-Ala, for the N-terminal end of the dipeptide, whereas a wide range of hydrophobic amino acids such as L-Phe, L-Tyr and L-Met are recognized for the C-terminal end. {ECO:0000269|PubMed:15609023, ECO:0000269|PubMed:16030213, ECO:0000269|PubMed:22407814, ECO:0000269|PubMed:23317005, ECO:0000269|PubMed:24702628}.

function: FUNCTION: L-amino acid ligase, which preferentially catalyzes the formation of L-aspartyl-L-methionine dipeptide from L-aspartate and L-methionine in the presence of ATP. Less active with L-asparagine and L-methionine as substrates. Less active with L-aspartate and either L-phenylalanine, L-valine, L-leucine or L-isoleucine as substrates. Decreased activity when L-methionine is substituted with seleno-DL-methionine, L-homocysteine, L-methionine sulfoxide, L-methionine sulfoximine and o-acetyl-L-serine. Decreased activity with acetylation of L-methionine amino group. Decreased activity by modification of L-methionine carboxylate to L-methionine methyl ester. No activity when L-methionine is substituted with L-homoserine. No activity with formylation of L-methionine amino group. No activity by modification of L-methionine carboxylate to L-methionine-glycine carboxylate. No activity when L-aspartate substrate is replaced by analogs such as L-homoserine, DL-aspartate beta-methyl ester, L-glutamate or o-acetyl-L-serine. No activity when L-aspartate amino and alpha-carboxylate groups are modified to L-malate, glycine-L-aspartate, L-aspartate-glycine or N-carbamoyl-DL-aspartate. No activity with L-methionine or L-aspartate as sole substrates. No activity in presence of other nucleoside triphosphates including GTP, CTP, UTP, TTP or ITP. Involved in sulfur amino acid metabolism. {ECO:0000269|PubMed:35988643}.
